name: Ocular Cicatricial Pemphigoid

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Immunopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Ocular Cicatricial Pemphigoid

criteria.description: Presence of chronic conjunctivitis with progressive conjunctival scarring
Positive direct immunofluorescence showing linear deposition of IgG, IgA, or C3 along the epithelial basement membrane zone
Exclusion of other causes of cicatrizing conjunctivitis such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome or chemical injury
Subepithelial blister formation with inflammatory infiltrate on conjunctival biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical features plus positive direct immunofluorescence and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by conjunctival biopsy with immunopathological studies.

searchTerms: scarring and thickening of eye surface

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symblepharon formation (adhesion between eyelid and eyeball)
searchTerms: adhesion between eyelid and eye surface

pathognomonic.symptomName: Subepithelial linear deposition of immunoglobulins at basement membrane zone
searchTerms: immune deposits under eye surface layer
antibody buildup at eye basement membrane

common.symptomName: Chronic conjunctival inflammation with redness and irritation
Dry eye syndrome due to lacrimal gland involvement
searchTerms: dry eyes from tear gland problems
lack of tears causing eye dryness
dry eye syndrome due to gland issues

occasional.symptomName: Visual impairment secondary to corneal scarring
searchTerms: eye sight affected by corneal damage

occasional.symptomName: Mucous membrane involvement outside the eye (oral, nasal)
searchTerms: mucous membrane problems in mouth or nose
inflammation of oral and nasal linings
reduced space between eyelid and eyeball

rare.symptomName: Secondary glaucoma due to angle closure
searchTerms: increased eye pressure from blocked drainage
secondary glaucoma due to eye angle problems

laboratory: Direct immunofluorescence of conjunctival biopsy showing linear IgG, IgA, or C3 deposition
Elevated inflammatory markers may be present but nonspecific
imaging: Slit-lamp examination revealing conjunctival scarring and symblepharon
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (OCT) may show conjunctival fibrosis
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; autoimmune pathogenesis
other: Histopathology showing subepithelial blister with inflammatory infiltrate
Clinical exclusion of other cicatrizing conjunctivitis causes

distinguishingFeatures: History of acute mucocutaneous reaction with skin involvement
Response to antibiotics and anti-inflammatory treatment
Acute onset with corneal epithelial defects

redFlags: Rapid progression of conjunctival scarring leading to vision loss
Development of symblepharon causing restricted eye movement
Corneal ulceration with risk of perforation
references: Chan LS, Ahmed AR, Anhalt GJ, et al. The first international consensus on mucous membrane pemphigoid: definition, diagnostic criteria, pathogenic factors, medical treatment, and prognostic indicators. Arch Dermatol. 2002;138(3):370-379.
Leonardi A, Fregona IA, Bortolotti M, et al. Ocular cicatricial pemphigoid: clinical features and treatment. Eye (Lond). 2016;30(2):224-231.
Williams GP, Dart JK. Ocular cicatricial pemphigoid. Eye (Lond). 2016;30(2):224-231.
